evals.name: python-native-workflow-store-and-hardcoded-key
evals.prompt: Before we deploy the travel concierge agent in ./travel-concierge-python, check its state store and memory configuration. It's a dapr-agents project.
evals.expected_output: A review-agent-memory report with Language: python. Critical DAG-MEM-001 because resources/agent-workflow.yaml has no actorStateStore: "true"; warning DAG-MEM-003 for the plain-text OpenAI key in resources/llm-provider.yaml; warning DAG-MEM-006 because the DurableAgent in main.py has no state=AgentStateConfig(...). ConversationListMemory in examples/local_demo.py (marked dev-only) is downgraded to Please verify. agent-memory.yaml is correct and not flagged.
expectations: The report section (after the optional one-line `Reviewing <path>` scope echo) starts with `# Dapr review — review-agent-memory` and contains `Language: python`
Under `## Critical` the report contains [DAG-MEM-001] citing resources/agent-workflow.yaml (any line 1-14) for the missing actorStateStore: "true"
Under `## Warnings` the report contains [DAG-MEM-003] citing resources/llm-provider.yaml:9 or :10 for the hardcoded key, with a Fix that uses `{{OPENAI_API_KEY}}` templating or a secretKeyRef
Under `## Warnings` the report contains [DAG-MEM-006] citing travel-concierge-agent/main.py (the DurableAgent( at line 9) for the missing state=AgentStateConfig(...)
DAG-MEM-002 for ConversationListMemory in travel-concierge-agent/examples/local_demo.py appears under `## Please verify`, NOT under `## Critical`
The report does NOT contain DAG-MEM-007 for resources/agent-memory.yaml (actorStateStore is "false"), DAG-MEM-008 (single-agent project, no registry), or DAG-MEM-005 for main.py (it passes memory=)
The report ends with a `## Next steps` section with no text after it, and the transcript shows only Read, Grep and Glob calls (no Write, Edit or Bash)

evals.name: dotnet-sessionless-invoker-and-package-floor
evals.prompt: Our helpdesk agent in helpdesk-dotnet (Microsoft Agent Framework + Diagrid.AI.Microsoft.AgentFramework) forgets everything between /ask calls. Can you review its memory and persistence setup?
evals.expected_output: A review-agent-memory report with Language: dotnet. DAG-MEM-005 for invoker.RunAgentAsync in Program.cs called without an AgentSession and with no CreateSessionAsync/AttachSession anywhere. DAG-MEM-006 for Microsoft.Extensions.AI pinned at 10.1.0 (below 10.6.0). The explicit Dapr.Workflow 1.18.10 reference, the context.RunAgentAsync calls inside TicketWorkflow, and the absence of agent-memory.yaml are not findings.
expectations: The report section (after the optional one-line `Reviewing <path>` scope echo) starts with `# Dapr review — review-agent-memory` and contains `Language: dotnet`
The report contains [DAG-MEM-005] citing HelpdeskApp/Program.cs:30 (invoker.RunAgentAsync without a session), with a Fix mentioning CreateSessionAsync and AttachSession
The report contains [DAG-MEM-006] citing HelpdeskApp/HelpdeskApp.csproj:11 for Microsoft.Extensions.AI 10.1.0 being below 10.6.0
The report does NOT flag the Dapr.Workflow 1.18.10 reference (HelpdeskApp.csproj:10) under DAG-MEM-006 and does not recommend removing it
The report does NOT cite HelpdeskApp/Workflows/TicketWorkflow.cs for DAG-MEM-005 (the context.RunAgentAsync calls on lines 13 and 17 are one-shot workflow agent runs)

The report does NOT treat the missing resources/agent-memory.yaml as a finding, and contains no DAG-MEM-001 (agent-workflow.yaml has actorStateStore "true") and no DAG-MEM-003 (the key is `{{ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}}`)
The report uses no Python-only rule ids (DAG-MEM-002, DAG-MEM-008), and the transcript shows no Write, Edit or Bash calls

evals.name: dotnet-clean-single-agent-no-findings
evals.prompt: review agent memory for faq-bot-dotnet. there's no agent-memory.yaml in resources and no Dapr.Workflow package in the csproj, is that a problem?
evals.expected_output: The project matches the create-agent-dotnet single-agent scaffold: agent-workflow.yaml with actorStateStore "true", templated LLM key, Diagrid.AI.Microsoft.AgentFramework 1.2.0 only, and a session created with CreateSessionAsync / reattached with AttachSession. The report body is `No issues found.` followed by Next steps; neither the missing agent-memory.yaml nor the missing explicit Dapr.Workflow reference is reported.
expectations: The report section (after the optional one-line `Reviewing <path>` scope echo) starts with `# Dapr review — review-agent-memory` and contains `Language: dotnet`
The report body contains `No issues found.` and no finding bullets (no `[DAG-MEM-` entries)
The `Found:` line reports 0 critical, 0 warnings, 0 suggestions and 0 to verify
The report does not describe the missing agent-memory.yaml or the missing explicit Dapr.Workflow package reference as a problem
The report ends with a `## Next steps` section that suggests running review-agent-tools, and no text follows it
No Write, Edit or Bash calls appear in the transcript and no fixture file is modified
